notes.author: human:pioootrek
notes.text: Owner wants a human or existing LLM client to commit/push and request build/tests on a remote worker, then retrieve evidence without manual SSH or copying logs. Prioritize this concrete remote-work experiment before autonomous fleet execution; commercial hosting and a complete forum are not prerequisites.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Linked docs/environment-runtime-plan.md and imported Secret Runtime v2 source note. Remote requests select an authorized profile; worker-side secret resolution is a separate access boundary. Secret-free remote checks do not wait for a vault, while credentialed runs require explicit trusted-code and grant policy.

notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: The product must support self-hosting and be prepared for an owner-operated SaaS. Requested a saved staged plan with validation that catches failures early.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: NOTE-20260909-self-hosted-saas-plan/implementation-plan.md records the proposed implementation and gates: address/HTTPS contracts, authenticated remote execution, organization isolation and deployment/restore acceptance. HTTPS owns stage 1; remote execution requires minimum authorization before networking and precedes public multi-tenant hosting. Customer-owned execution is a proposed initial boundary. Planning only; this feature remains open.

notes.author: human:pioootrek
notes.text: Requested the implementation plan; expects the worker to fetch/update project code to the requested commit automatically when needed.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Detailed plan at NOTE-20260909-self-hosted-saas-plan/remote-verification-implementation.md (baseline d429eb9): six gated slices from durable identity/grants through worker-owned exact-SHA preparation, existing queue integration, outbound dispatch/recovery, MCP/CLI/UI, and installation acceptance. Automatic source fetching uses isolated attempt workspaces; never moves active worktrees or substitutes branch HEAD. Early tests cover authorization, source drift, dependency setup, duplicate delivery, offline cancellation, restarts and retention. Planning only; next implementation slice is identity/grants/state contracts.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Implementation resumed on t3code/remote-commit-verification by integrating the previously reviewed remote contracts, SQLite persistence, exact-SHA workspace and attempt-state series with current main. The integration preserves the main-line launch-preset repair and adds a regression-tested migration path for databases opened on the pre-merge remote branch. Focused tests, pnpm check and pnpm build pass. This is not feature completion: one-time enrollment, credential hashes/expiry/revocation, versioned worker protocol, queue execution and transports remain open.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Reconciled main 17d0c9d7e5be6d3f451298cdb7b364dbf25f5200: remote-verification service/contracts, SQLite requests/attempts and exact-SHA workspace preparation are already merged, with focused tests. No complete remote worker transport/runner is wired into CLI, HTTP or MCP. Remaining work: enrollment and revocable worker credentials, a versioned outbound protocol, integration with finite-job execution, reconnect/cancel/recovery behavior, caller transports and an exact-SHA owner trial. Earlier instructions to begin slice 1 are historical.

problem: Remote request authorization/persistence, attempt transitions and exact-SHA workspace preparation exist, but there is no end-to-end connected-worker execution workflow. Enrollment, dispatch, queue execution, reconciliation and caller transports remain to be integrated.

risk.rollback: Keep remote dispatch opt-in and independent of existing local verification. Disable new submissions, reconcile or explicitly cancel accepted attempts, preserve logs/run metadata, and revoke worker credentials without claiming disconnected processes have stopped.

scope: Implement docs/remote-verification-plan.md in bounded slices after urgent reliability repairs; begin with one trusted project and owner-controlled worker.

Extend existing queue/process abstractions to fetch an authorized exact commit into a separate run workspace and execute configured build/unit-test/lint/typecheck presets. Record actual SHA, preset/environment fingerprint, and setup/execution outcomes.

Provide scoped outbound worker connectivity and shared submission/status contracts for MCP, CLI, and web. Keep workers authoritative over local limits and credentials; accept no arbitrary remote shell commands or paths.
Persist idempotent submissions, explicit attempts, disconnect/restart reconciliation, and cancellation evidence without automatic redispatch of uncertain work.
Keep SaaS optional, execution customer-owned, and browser suites, autonomous agent launch, and operator-hosted untrusted execution deferred.
title: Run verification of pushed commits on customer-owned remote workers
validation: Fixture repositories prove exact SHA execution despite branch advancement, and reject missing or unauthorized source/presets without branch fallback.

Verify duplicate submit, disconnect/restart, uncertain attempts, stale reports, descendant cancellation, capacity, setup failures, cache separation, bounded output, and cleanup preserving unrelated workspaces.
Run a real owner workflow: existing LLM client submits a failing pushed commit, reads remote evidence, then submits a corrected revision with separately attributable results.
Verify credential revocation, output access scopes, recoverable run metadata, and honest artifact expiry without exposing secrets.
Remote finite verification does not move an active development worktree or bypass local runtime reservations/resource policies.
value: The owner can work with an LLM from a lightweight device while a prepared worker performs expensive checks.
Trustworthy reusable remote execution is proven before investing in autonomous fleets or commercial hosted runners.
